original_question: Give a geometric characterization of zero sets of H p functions on strongly pseudoconvex domains.
target_in_paper: The nearest official target is the unnumbered open problem in The Several Complex Variables Problem List asking for a geometric characterization of zero sets of H^p-functions on strongly/strictly pseudoconvex domains.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core subject: Hardy-space zero sets, the several-complex-variables setting, and the fact that the issue is to find a geometric characterization on strongly pseudoconvex domains rather than merely a sufficient condition.
missing_details: The ambient space should be specified: a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^n.
The boundary regularity should be stated; the standard background result used here is for bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains with smooth (in Varopoulos, C^4) boundary.
In several variables, the relevant object is not just a set but an effective divisor/analytic hypersurface, with multiplicities counted.
It should be made explicit whether p > 0 is fixed in advance or whether one asks for existence of some p > 0; this matters because for n ≥ 2 the zero divisors can depend on p.
A stand-alone formulation should say whether the characterization is meant to be necessary and sufficient.
A global topological obstruction should be acknowledged: for a divisor to be the zero divisor of a global holomorphic function, its canonical cohomology class in H^2(Ω; ℤ) must vanish.
The question should clarify whether it asks for characterization of exact zero divisors of functions F ∈ H^p(Ω), not merely subsets of zero sets.

The paper-faithful context suggests that any eventual characterization should refine the ordinary Blaschke condition by a boundary-uniform condition of Carleson/uniform-Blaschke type, so leaving all boundary-growth content implicit makes the draft underspecified.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded smoothly bounded strictly (strongly) pseudoconvex domain, and fix p > 0. Give necessary and sufficient geometric conditions on an effective divisor M in Ω, with multiplicities counted and including any indispensable topological obstruction such as the vanishing of its canonical class in H^2(Ω; ℤ), for there to exist a holomorphic function F ∈ H^p(Ω) whose zero divisor is exactly M.
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is itself a problem list rather than a theorem-style paper, so the closest paper-faithful target is the corresponding unnumbered open problem, not a numbered conjecture or theorem. Your draft is already very close to that target, but it is not fully stand-alone because in several complex variables 'zero set' really means a divisor/hypersurface with multiplicities, the domain should be bounded and smoothly bounded in ℂ^n, and one must decide whether p is fixed or existential. The nearby mathematical context for what such a characterization is supposed to refine comes from Varopoulos: the ordinary Blaschke condition characterizes Nevanlinna zero sets on strictly pseudoconvex domains, while for H^p one needs a stronger boundary-uniform condition, and in addition there is a canonical cohomology-class obstruction for representing a divisor as the zero divisor of a global holomorphic function.
